newsitem.title: USA: Wis. unemployment falls to 3.4 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Wis. unemployment falls to 3.4 pct in April.

text.p: Wisconsin's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate dropped to 3.4 percent in April from 3.5 percent in March, the state's workforce development department reported Tuesday.
It was the sixth straight April that the unemployment rate improved in Wisconsin, where it had been 5.6 percent in 1991, the department pointed out.

Job growth in the last 12 months has been most rapid in the Eau Claire-Chippewa Falls area in western Wisconsin and the Janesville-Beloit area on the state's southern border with Illinois experienced the only actual job loss in that period, the department reported.
The U.S. unemployment rate dropped from 5.2 percent in March to 4.9 percent in April.
